Understanding CPCB vs US EPA AQI (Why AQI.in shows 109 while CPCB shows 53–65)

Architecture Overview End-to-End System Flow

End-to-End System Architecture: How It Works

A clear, step-by-step visual walkthrough of how live telemetry, atmospheric sounding physics, machine learning ensembles, and ground-truth calibration combine to produce 72-hour air quality forecasts.

1. Computational Pipeline: From Raw Sensors to Final Policy

Step 1 15-Min Ingestion
Multimodal Ingestion

Pulls from 6 live streams: 24 CPCB stations, IMD Safdarjung soundings, GFS weather, NASA VIIRS fires, TomTom traffic, and EDGAR emissions.

Input: Raw Sensor Feeds
Step 2 148 Features
Physics Engine

Calculates physical atmosphere parameters: Inversion Lid (ΔT), Ventilation Index (VI), Boundary Layer Height (PBLH), and 315° NW fire plume lag.

Formula: VI = PBLH × Wind
Step 3 R² up to 0.9235 (+72h up to 0.7450)
AI Convex Ensemble

Tri-model blend: Ridge (near-term inertia), LightGBM (diurnal weather cycles), and XGBoost (fire plumes). Weighted by NNLS convex optimization.

Blend: min ||Y - Vw||²
Step 4 τ = 18 Hours
Ground Calibration

Applies exponential error relaxation to match real CAAQMS ground truth at t=0 while smoothly transitioning to physics grid as lead time expands.

Relax: C + e₀ · exp(-t/18h)
Step 5 Actionable Output
Decision Support

Generates 676 3km grid cell maps, aggregates 16 NCR administrative zones, triggers statutory CAQM GRAP I-IV alerts, and drives VayuMitra.

Output: Maps & GRAP Stage

2. The Machine Learning Engine: Why We Blend 3 Models

1. Ridge Regression (L2) Dominates +1h to +6h

Why it is used: Air quality has high physical inertia. In the next 1 to 3 hours, tomorrow's weather changes matter much less than the smoke currently suspended in the air. Ridge regression models linear persistence reliably without overfitting noisy fluctuations.

Weight in Ensemble: ~80% at +1h • Role: Immediate physical persistence
2. LightGBM (Gradient Trees) Dominates +24h to +72h

Why it is used: Over 24 to 72 hours, linear persistence fades and meteorology takes command. LightGBM captures non-linear day/night cycles, boundary layer solar heating expansion, wind vector shifts, and photochemical ozone reactions.

Weight in Ensemble: ~81% at +72h • Role: Long-term weather & diurnal cycle
3. XGBoost (Regularized Trees) Extreme Events & Plumes

Why it is used: Stubble burning plumes and severe winter inversions are non-linear threshold events. XGBoost models complex multi-parameter interactions between satellite fire power, wind steering angle (315° NW corridor), and cold stagnant air.

Weight in Ensemble: ~15-20% • Role: Transboundary stubble & cross-interactions
Convex Non-Negative Least Squares (NNLS) Optimizer

The ensemble computes optimal weights for each lead hour (+1h to +72h) such that weights are non-negative and sum to exactly 100%. This guarantees no model hallucinates and maximizes prediction R² up to 0.9235 (and up to 0.7450 at +72h).

min_w ||Y - Vw||²  s.t.  w_i ≥ 0, Σw_i = 1

3. Atmospheric Physics: Why Air Pollution Traps Over Delhi NCR

Above 1,000m Free Troposphere (Clean Air Aloft)
Warm air aloft • Rapid wind dispersion
Thermal Inversion Lid The "Airtight Glass Ceiling" (ΔT = +8.0 K)

Warm air sits on top of cold surface air, acting like a closed lid. Diagnosed via IMD Safdarjung Radiosonde Station 42182 soundings.

Locks Smoke Below
Ground to 250m Trapped Nocturnal Boundary Layer (PBLH < 250m)

Cold, stagnant surface air where vehicle exhaust, dust, and stubble fire plumes accumulate with nowhere to escape.

Ventilation Index < 300 m²/s
Ground Surface: 24 CPCB CAAQMS Monitoring Stations
Continuous 15-Min Telemetry
The 3 Drivers of Delhi Severe Smog
1. Nocturnal Radiation Cooling: At night, Delhi's land cools rapidly. The cold air stays near the ground while warmer air stays aloft, creating an inversion layer that blocks vertical ventilation.
2. Low Ventilation Index (VI): Ventilation Index equals boundary layer height multiplied by wind speed. When wind drops below 2 m/s, VI drops below 1,000 m²/s, causing pollution concentrations to spike.
3. 315° NW Stubble Fire Corridor: Post-monsoon winds blow from Punjab/Haryana toward Delhi. Smoke takes 12 to 24 hours to travel down the corridor, dumping fine aerosols straight into the trapped basin.

4. Ground-Truth Calibration: How We Match Station Realities

The Challenge: Regional Grids vs. Roadside Monitors

A 3x3 km satellite or weather model cell covers an entire neighborhood. However, a ground station (like Anand Vihar) sits next to a highway and bus terminal, measuring immediate local spikes. Standard ML models either over-predict the neighborhood or under-predict the station.

Our Solution: 18-Hour Exponential Error Assimilation

At lead time = 0h, the forecast matches the station's exact live measurement. As the forecast steps forward into tomorrow, the station offset smoothly relaxes back to the regional physics grid with an 18-hour decay timescale (half-life of 12.5 hours).

Formula: C_corrected(t) = C_grid(t) + [ C_station(0) - C_grid(0) ] × exp(-t / 18h)

1. Multi-Target Ensemble Architecture & Maximized R² Benchmark Matrix

Strictly validated on held-out test records (Nov-Dec 2024 severe episode). Compares Persistence Baseline, Ridge Regression, XGBoost, LightGBM, and the Optimized Blended Ensemble.

A. Constrained Convex Blending

Ensemble weights are optimized via Non-Negative Least Squares (NNLS) on the validation split: min_w ||Y - V w||² s.t. w_i ≥ 0, Σw_i = 1 Combines LightGBM histogram gradient trees, regularized XGBoost, and bounded Ridge regression.

B. Receptor Residual Bias Decay

Station ground-truth measurements assimilate directly through an 18-hour exponential relaxation: C_corr(t) = C_grid(t) + e0 · exp(-t / 18h) Eliminates spatial representativeness errors at complex urban monitoring receptors.

C. Piecewise Segmented CPCB NAQI

Standardized statutory conversion mapping raw mass concentrations into normalized sub-indices: Ip = I_low + [(I_hi - I_low)/(B_hi - B_low)]·(Cp - B_low) Final composite AQI is strictly driven by the maximum sub-index (Prominent Pollutant).

Pollutant Lead Hour Persistence R² Ridge R² XGBoost R² LightGBM R² Maximized Ensemble R² MAE RMSE Optimized Ensemble Blend

2. Multimodal Data Ingestion Pipelines & Unified Dataset Catalog

1. CPCB CAAQMS Telemetry 15-Min Live

Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Network covering 24 statutory ground receptors across NCT Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Noida, and Ghaziabad. Ingests PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, and NH3 under CPCB/DPCC regulatory QA/QC.

Protocol: Open Government Data (data.gov.in) API • Ingestion Latency: < 1.2s • Fallback: Calibrated Operational Cache.
2. IMD Radiosonde Soundings 00 & 12 UTC

Official India Meteorological Department (IMD) Station 42182 Safdarjung atmospheric soundings. Captures mandatory vertical profiles from 1000 hPa to 500 hPa to diagnose real thermodynamic temperature inversions (ΔT = T925 - T1000 K).

Key Metrics: Inversion Strength (K), Brunt-Väisälä N², Potential Temperature Lapse Rate (∂θ/∂z), Inversion Lid Presence.
3. NCMRWF & GFS NWP (0.25°) 0.25° Gridded

Coupled numerical weather prediction simulation providing 72-hour forward meteorological trajectories: 10m horizontal wind vectors (u, v), Planetary Boundary Layer Height (PBLH), sensible heat flux, total cloud cover, and surface pressure.

Derived Diagnostics: Ventilation Index (VI = PBLH × U10 in m²/s), Stagnation Indicator, Rain Wet-Deposition Scavenging.
4. NASA VIIRS & MODIS Satellites 375m Thermal

Real-time agricultural stubble fire thermal anomalies across Punjab, Haryana, Western UP, and Rajasthan (24°-34°N, 72°-81°E). Measures Fire Radiative Power (FRP in Megawatts) and wind-aligned distance decay advection corridors.

Lag Engine: Plume transit lag hours (8h to 24h) calculated along prevailing 315° North-West atmospheric steering corridor.
5. EDGAR v8.1 Global Emissions 0.1° Gridded

High-resolution anthropogenic atmospheric emission inventory disaggregated across specific economic sectors: road transportation, thermal energy utilities, heavy industrial fabrication, and residential cooking/biofuel combustion.

Coverage: 6,084 km² NCR domain • Source Attribution: Road exhaust (42%), Dust (28%), Industry (18%), Domestic (12%).
6. Real-Time Traffic Telemetry 16 Corridors

Multi-corridor live traffic flow and travel time delays ingested across Outer Ring Road, NH-48, GT Road, DND Flyway, and expressway corridors. Computes the domain Traffic Congestion Factor (TCF%) and dynamic exhaust emission multipliers.

Coupling Factor: Multiplier scales from 1.0x (free flow) to 1.6x (standstill gridlock) updating local NOx and PM2.5 injection.

3. Complete Feature Engineering & Physics Feature Catalog (148 Features)

A. Autoregressive Temporal Lags (48 Features)

Multi-scale lag observations for each criteria pollutant: t-1h, t-2h, t-3h, t-6h, t-12h, t-24h, t-48h, t-72h. Provides memory of baseline concentration history and chemical persistence.

B. Rolling Inertia & Volatility (36 Features)

Rolling temporal mean windows (6h, 12h, 24h, 48h, 72h) and rolling standard deviation (24h std) measuring local airshed inertia, diurnal variance, and sudden wind flushing events.

C. Chemical & Photochemical Ratios (6 Features)

Diagnostic chemical ratios: PM2.5 / PM10 ratio (distinguishes secondary combustion aerosols from coarse mineral dust) and NO2 / O3 ratio (tracks daytime photochemical ozone titration).

D. Boundary Layer Thermodynamics (24 Features)

Direct physical features from IMD Radiosonde and GFS: Planetary Boundary Layer Height (PBLH), Inversion Cap (ΔT K), Ventilation Index (VI = PBLH × U10), Brunt-Väisälä stability (N²).

E. Agricultural Fire Plume Transport (20 Features)

Upwind radial fire counts & FRP within 25 km, 50 km, 100 km, 200 km rings; Punjab/Haryana exponentially weighted FRP (12h, 24h, 48h); Northwest steering wind alignment cosine score (cos(θ - 315°)).

F. Continuous Harmonic Cyclic Encodings (8 Features)

Trigonometric sine and cosine transformations of hour of day (sin_hour, cos_hour), day of week (sin_dow, cos_dow), and day of year (sin_doy, cos_doy) guaranteeing cyclic boundary continuity.

4. Comprehensive Dashboard Operations Guide (Tab-by-Tab User Manual)

1 Operating Tab 1: 3 km Spatial Grid Forecast & Live Telemetry

• Timeline Slider & Play Button: Scrub through lead hours (+1h, +3h, +6h, +12h, +24h, +36h, +48h, +72h) or click the Play/Pause button to run the automatic forward forecast sequence at 2.2-second steps.

• Live CPCB Telemetry Sync: Click the "Sync Live CPCB Data" button right on the header bar to immediately pull real-time CAAQMS data from data.gov.in. Set the cadence dropdown (1m, 3m, 5m, 10m, Off) to automate background refresh with live countdown.

• Interactive Map Layer Controls: Toggle the spatial metric buttons (AQI, PM2.5, PM10, Inversion Lid, Ventilation Index) to re-render the 676 grid polygons. Toggle the Traffic Flow button to superimpose real-time TomTom vehicle congestion speed corridors.

• Receptor & Cell Inspection: Click any of the 676 grid polygons or 24 monitoring pins to populate the right-hand Inspector Card with radial AQI gauge, prominent pollutant, and criteria pollutant sub-indices.

2 Operating Tab 2: Administrative Zones & CAQM GRAP Decision Support

• Zone Aggregation: Inspect how 676 underlying 3km cells aggregate into 16 NCR administrative jurisdictions with P90 vulnerable exposure and corridor traffic delays.

• GRAP Action Stages: Review triggered Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) Graded Response Action Plan stages (Stage I Poor ≥ 201, Stage II Very Poor ≥ 301, Stage III Severe ≥ 401, Stage IV Severe+ ≥ 450).

• Counterfactual Policy Simulator: Check or uncheck regulatory restriction toggles (Truck Ban, Construction Halt, Sweeping, DG Sets Ban, Staggered Offices, Smart Corridor Diversion) to re-simulate immediate air quality improvements.

3 Operating Tab 3: Regional Source & Agricultural Fire Transport

• Transboundary Plume Monitoring: Observes satellite thermal fire detections and total Fire Radiative Power (MW) across Punjab, Haryana, Western UP, and Rajasthan.

• Corridor Advection Matrix: Inspect geodesic distance to Delhi, transport azimuth (315° NW corridor), boundary layer wind alignment, transit lag hours, and airshed attribution share.

4 Operating Tab 4: CPCB Station Ground-Truth Validation & Bias Correction

• Ground-Truth Receptor Benchmarking: Directly evaluates raw uncalibrated numerical model grid outputs against real-time 24 CPCB CAAQMS stations.

• 18-Hour Exponential Relaxation: Displays initial error bias (e0 = Observed - Raw Grid) and the bias-corrected 24h forward forecast calibrated via C_corr = C_grid + e0 · exp(-t / 18h).

5 Operating Tab 5: Past 1-Year Historical CAAQMS Telemetry

• 365-Day Searchable Records: Search by date or keyword, filter by official CPCB AQI health categories (Good to Severe), and paginate through 365 daily observations covering an entire annual atmospheric cycle.

6 Operating Floating VayuMitra: Conversational Air Quality Companion

• Persistent Floating Launcher: Click the pill button in the bottom-right corner to open the conversational AI desk. Ask questions in simple language regarding weather traps, GRAP bans, health safety, or forecast accuracy.

Why CPCB and AQI.in Show Different Numbers

Indian National AQI (CPCB NAQI) vs United States EPA AQI
Physical Sensor Measurement is 100% Identical

Both our system and consumer apps like AQI.in, Apple Weather, and Google Weather measure the exact same particulate concentration (e.g. PM2.5 = 39.0 µg/m³). The difference in the reported AQI number is purely due to which mathematical formula is applied.

Exact Mathematical Calculation for PM2.5 = 39.0 µg/m³

1. US EPA AQI (AQI.in, iOS)
109 (Poor)

Breakpoint [35.5 - 55.4 µg/m³] maps to [101 - 150 AQI]:
101 + ((39.0-35.5)/(55.4-35.5))*49 = 109.6 ≈ 109

2. Indian CPCB NAQI (Official)
65 (Satisfactory)

Breakpoint [30.0 - 60.0 µg/m³] maps to [51 - 100 AQI]:
50 + ((39.0-30.0)/(60.0-30.0))*50 = 65

PM2.5 (µg/m³) Indian CPCB Category CPCB AQI US EPA Category US EPA AQI
0 – 30 Good 0 – 50 Good (≤12) / Mod 0 – 89
31 – 60 (Current: 39) Satisfactory 51 – 100 Poor (Sensitive) 91 – 153
61 – 90 Moderate 101 – 200 Unhealthy 154 – 169
91 – 120 Poor 201 – 300 Unhealthy 170 – 184
121 – 250 Very Poor 301 – 400 Very Unhealthy 185 – 300

Why is the Indian scale calibrated this way? The Indian National AQI was established by an expert group convened by MoEFCC and CPCB (IIT Kanpur, NEERI, AIIMS) taking into account the natural background mineral dust and ambient climatic conditions of the Indo-Gangetic Plain. Commercial apps default to the United States EPA breakpoint table.
